note: Four open chords as a loop, in three sections: the shapes in the order of the loop, down strums on every beat, then the same strums with beat 1 a little harder. The why says what a loop does for the hand; each step names the beat to move on and what to do when a change is late.

exercise.title: G, Em, C and D as a loop
exercise.why: G, Em, C and D go round as a loop, so each chord always changes to the same next chord and your hand has four changes to learn, the same four every time round.

cells.text:
Press a chord box below to hear the chord. The boxes are in the order of the loop: G, Em, C, then D, and after D the loop starts again on G.
Fret each chord in turn and strum it once, slowly.
Go round until the change from Em to C is as quick as the other three.

Press Play below to start the metronome at {{=bpm}}. After a bar of count-in, the lit box shows the chord to play. Strum down on every beat, one bar for each chord, and start moving your fingers to the next chord on beat 4.
If a change comes late, keep your strumming hand going and catch the next beat 1.

Press Play below to start the metronome. Play the same loop with the same strums, and strum beat 1 of every bar a little harder than beats 2, 3 and 4.
Listen for the start of each bar standing out, so you can hear where each chord begins.
